label: r3c1
name: Column-skip + dilated context conv
hypothesis: Adds a third residual 3x3 conv with dilation 2 to r1c2. The receptive field grows from 5x5 to about 9x9, which covers the whole 8x8 grid. The agent can then see distant missing cells and the supports an overhang needs, which governs the safe build order, and DONE and value get better features. Cost is about r=1.35. Refuted if it scores no better than r1c2. That would mean decisions are local and the samples it costs are wasted.
last_analysis: Scores are hidden, so these choices come from reasoning, not measured results. All earlier trials trained without errors. The column-skip head is the most plausible network gain because it costs almost nothing (r≈1.08). The costlier options (attention, per-layer head, wider head) leave fewer training samples. Exact-build success depends on the +1 bonus at episode end, which gamma 0.95 heavily discounts, so gamma 0.99 with lambda 0.95 is the recipe change most likely to help. Fewer PPO epochs (2) give about 1.8x more fresh designs, which should help generalisation. In this last round I combine these plausible gains: (A) column-skip with long horizon and the sample-heavy recipe; (B) dilated full-grid context with long horizon; (C) a new idea, the legality mask reshaped to per-type maps and fed in as learned input, which hints at landing height near the top of the stack, with long horizon.
